extracted.intended_audience: Users of GAP (computational group theorists and mathematicians) working with character tables
extracted.subtask_description: Reference-manual-level descriptions of GAP operations and attributes for constructing, identifying, querying, and analyzing character tables and their relation to groups; includes requirements, returned formats, and invariants used for consistency and identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: CharacterTableWithStoredGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: CharacterTableWithStoredGroup(G, tbl[, info]) — Given a group G and a character table tbl of a group isomorphic to G (when G does not already store its OrdinaryCharacterTable), try to identify the classes of G with the columns of tbl and, if identification is unique up to automorphisms of tbl, store tbl as the CharacterTable value of G and return a new equivalent table with UnderlyingGroup, ConjugacyClasses, and IdentificationOfConjugacyClasses set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If identification is not unique up to automorphisms of tbl, fail is returned. If a record info is present it has the same meaning as the optional arec argument for CompatibleConjugacyClasses. If a list is given as third argument it is used as IdentificationOfConjugacyClasses value of G without further checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: CompatibleConjugacyClasses
rubrics_metrics.description: CompatibleConjugacyClasses([G, ccl,] tbl[, arec]) — Identify which columns of the character table tbl correspond to which conjugacy classes of G (or of a group isomorphic to the table's group). Returns a list l with l[i] = position in ccl of class corresponding to i-th column of tbl if identification is unique up to table automorphisms; otherwise returns fail (or a list of indistinguishable class-position sets in the second form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical usage: call the second form first to check quickly whether the first form can succeed. Invariants used for identification: (1) element orders (OrdersClassRepresentatives), (2) class lengths (SizesConjugacyClasses), (3) power maps (PowerMap / ComputedPowerMaps), (4) symmetries of the table (AutomorphismsOfTable). Optional arec record supports additional info: natchar (values of the natural character), bijection (partial bijection giving positions). Returned list is empty exactly when identification is unique under invariants used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infix operators for character tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Infix operators defined: tbl1 * tbl2 (direct product of two character tables), tbl / list (table of factor group modulo normal subgroup spanned by classes in list), tbl mod p (p-modular Brauer character table corresponding to ordinary tbl), tbl.name (position of class with given name in tbl).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operators map to operations: CharacterTableDirectProduct, CharacterTableFactorGroup, BrauerTable, and ClassNames(Class lookup). Use tbl.name to access class position by class name.

rubrics_metrics.name: CharacterDegrees
rubrics_metrics.description: CharacterDegrees(G[, p]) / CharacterDegrees(tbl) — returns a collected list of degrees of the absolutely irreducible characters of the group G (or of the character table tbl). Optional p is 0 or a prime indicating the characteristic; default 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For groups the default method delegates to the tbl call. For solvable groups a specific default method based on Con90b is used. Example outputs show collected multiplicities: e.g. [ [1,2], [2,1], [3,2] ].

rubrics_metrics.name: Irr
rubrics_metrics.description: Irr(G[, p]) / Irr(tbl) — returns the irreducible characters of the ordinary character table of G (or the p-modular Brauer irreducibles when p supplied); for a character table tbl returns the list of all complex absolutely irreducible characters of tbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordering of columns in the Irr matrix for a group G refers to conjugacy class ordering in the CharacterTable value of G, which may differ from ordering in G; ordering of Irr need not coincide with ordering of IrreducibleRepresentations. For p-solvable groups p-modular irreducibles may be computed via Fong–Swan; otherwise no method may be available. Examples show difference between ordinary and modular irr lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: LinearCharacters
rubrics_metrics.description: LinearCharacters(G[, p]) / LinearCharacters(tbl) — returns the linear (degree 1) characters from the Irr list of the group G or character table tbl; in second form returns p-modular linear characters when p provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordering of linear characters in tbl need not coincide with ordering of linear characters in irr list. Delegation rules similar to Irr (may delegate to group/table).

rubrics_metrics.name: OrdinaryCharacterTable
rubrics_metrics.description: OrdinaryCharacterTable(G) / OrdinaryCharacterTable(modtbl) — returns the ordinary character table of group G or of the Brauer character table modtbl, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brauer tables are constructed from ordinary tables so OrdinaryCharacterTable(modtbl) returns stored ordinary table. Example: OrdinaryCharacterTable(SymmetricGroup(4)) returns CharacterTable(Sym([1..4])).

rubrics_metrics.name: Group operations applicable to character tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Several group operations/attributes (Size, IsAbelian, IsSolvable, AbelianInvariants, CommutatorLength, Exponent, IsSimple, IsNilpotent, IsMonomial, IsPerfect, IsQuasisimple, IsSporadicSimple, IsSupersolvable, IsAlmostSimple, IsCyclic, IsElementaryAbelian, IsFinite, IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup, NrConjugacyClasses) are applicable to character tables and mean the same as for underlying groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operations are useful for selecting character tables with specified properties, including for tables without access to an underlying group. Examples show List(tables, IsAbelian), List(tables, Size), IsomorphismTypeInfoFiniteSimpleGroup(CharacterTable("C5")) etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: OrdersClassRepresentatives
rubrics_metrics.description: OrdersClassRepresentatives(tbl) — list of orders of representatives of conjugacy classes of the character table tbl, in the same ordering as the classes of tbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an invariant for class identification and consistency checks. Example: OrdersClassRepresentatives(CharacterTable("A5")) -> [1,2,3,5,5].

rubrics_metrics.name: SizesCentralizers
rubrics_metrics.description: SizesCentralizers(tbl) / SizesCentralisers(tbl) — list where position i stores the size of the centralizer of any element in the i-th conjugacy class of tbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for consistency and identification; example SizesCentralizers(CharacterTable("A5")) -> [60,4,3,5,5].

rubrics_metrics.name: SizesConjugacyClasses
rubrics_metrics.description: SizesConjugacyClasses(tbl) — list where position i stores the size of the i-th conjugacy class of tbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as invariant for identification; example SizesConjugacyClasses(CharacterTable("A5")) -> [1,15,20,12,12].

rubrics_metrics.name: AutomorphismsOfTable
rubrics_metrics.description: AutomorphismsOfTable(tbl) — permutation group of all column permutations of tbl that leave the set of irreducibles and each power map of tbl invariant (i.e., table automorphisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as invariant for CompatibleConjugacyClasses. Example: AutomorphismsOfTable(CharacterTable("Dihedral",8)) -> Group([ (4,5) ]).

rubrics_metrics.name: UnderlyingCharacteristic
rubrics_metrics.description: UnderlyingCharacteristic(tbl) / UnderlyingCharacteristic(psi) — returns 0 for ordinary character tables, p for p-modular Brauer tables; for class functions psi equals underlying characteristic of its underlying table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This attribute must be stored when the table is constructed; cannot be computed. Note: cannot use GAP's Characteristic attribute name for this; examples show 0 for ordinary and 17 for tbl mod 17.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassNames and CharacterNames
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassNames(tbl[, "ATLAS"]) and CharacterNames(tbl) — return lists of strings naming conjugacy classes and irreducible characters of tbl for display; defaults: class names generated from element orders plus letters, character names default to ["X.1","X.2",...].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When ClassNames called with "ATLAS" second arg, names follow Atlas conventions. Position lookup: tbl.name returns class position. Example: ClassNames(CharacterTable("A5")) -> ["1a","2a","3a","5a","5b"] and tbl.2a -> 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassParameters and CharacterParameters
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassParameters(tbl) and CharacterParameters(tbl) — lists containing a parameter for each conjugacy class or irreducible character of tbl; meaning depends on tbl (no default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For symmetric groups classes can be parametrized by partitions. Generic character tables constructed from library often have parameters stored. For p-modular Brauer tables class parameters may be returned for p-regular classes if stored in underlying ordinary table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifier (for character tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifier(tbl) — string identifying tbl in current GAP session; used for class fusions and printing tables (e.g., library tables get names like "A5" or default "CTn").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default ordinary method constructs strings of form "CTn" with n from LARGEST_IDENTIFIER_NUMBER; Brauer tables return concatenation of ordinary identifier, "mod", and underlying characteristic. Examples: Identifier(CharacterTable("A5")) -> "A5"; Identifier(tbl) -> "CT8".

rubrics_metrics.name: InfoText (for character tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: InfoText(tbl) — mutable string with information about tbl (origin, tests passed, choices made). No default method to create one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used mainly for library tables; usual parts include origin, tests (1.o.r., pow[p], DEC, TENS). Example prints: origin: ATLAS of finite groups, tests: 1.o.r., pow[2,3,5].

rubrics_metrics.name: InverseClasses
rubrics_metrics.description: InverseClasses(tbl) — list mapping each conjugacy class to its inverse class (i.e., the (-1)-st power map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computed from power maps; example InverseClasses(CharacterTable("A5")) -> [1,2,3,4,5].

rubrics_metrics.name: RealClasses
rubrics_metrics.description: RealClasses(tbl) — strictly sorted list of positions of classes in tbl that consist of real elements (elements conjugate to their inverse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computed via conjugacy and inverse relation; example RealClasses(CharacterTable("A5")) -> [1,2,3,4,5].

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassOrbit
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassOrbit(tbl, cc) — list of positions of conjugacy classes of tbl that are Galois conjugate to the cc-th class; computed from power maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents classes containing generators of the cyclic group generated by an element in cc-th class. Example ClassOrbit(CharacterTable("A5"),4) -> [4,5].

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassRoots
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassRoots(tbl) — list where position i gives list of positions of classes that are nontrivial p-th roots (for p prime divisors of Size(tbl)) of elements in i-th class; computed from power maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example outputs show nested lists; used for analyzing root relationships among classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfNormalSubgroups (and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfNormalSubgroups(ordtbl), ClassPositionsOfMaximalNormalSubgroups(ordtbl), ClassPositionsOfMinimalNormalSubgroups(ordtbl) — return strictly sorted lists of class positions (relative to ordtbl's ConjugacyClasses ordering) that correspond to normal subgroups (maximal/minimal) of the group of ordtbl; entries sorted by increasing length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These correspond to group-level NormalSubgroups, MaximalNormalSubgroups, MinimalNormalSubgroups. Sorting respects inclusion partial order by reporting lists in increasing length. Example: ClassPositionsOfNormalSubgroups(CharacterTable("Symmetric",4)) -> [ [1], [1,3], [1,3,4], [1..5] ].

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfAgemo
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfAgemo(ordtbl, p) — corresponds to Agemo for the group of the ordinary character table ordtbl; returns class positions forming the subgroup Agemo_p(G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example ClassPositionsOfAgemo(CharacterTable("Symmetric",4),2) -> [1,3,4].

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfCentre
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfCentre(ordtbl) / ClassPositionsOfCenter(ordtbl) — positions of classes forming the centre of the group of the ordinary character table ordtbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example ClassPositionsOfCentre(CharacterTable("Dihedral",8)) -> [1,3].

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfDirectProductDecompositions
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfDirectProductDecompositions(tbl[, nclasses]) — returns all pairs [l1,l2] of lists of class positions of normal subgroups N1,N2 such that underlying group is direct product N1 x N2 (|N1| ≤ |N2|). If nclasses given, returns decompositions of that normal subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to detect direct product structure from table data and class positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfDerivedSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfDerivedSubgroup(ordtbl) — positions of classes forming the derived subgroup of group for ordtbl (corresponds to DerivedSubgroup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example ClassPositionsOfDerivedSubgroup(CharacterTable("Dihedral",8)) -> [1,3].

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfElementaryAbelianSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfElementaryAbelianSeries(ordtbl) — returns list of lists of class positions corresponding to the elementary abelian series of the group of ordtbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries correspond to levels of series; may return fail for some tables. Example for SymmetricGroup(4) yields nested lists, while CharacterTable("A5") may fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfFittingSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfFittingSubgroup(ordtbl) — class positions corresponding to the Fitting subgroup of the group of ordtbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example ClassPositionsOfFittingSubgroup(CharacterTable("Symmetric",4)) -> [1,3].

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfLowerCentralSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfLowerCentralSeries(tbl) — returns list of lists of class positions corresponding to the lower central series of the group of tbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example outputs for SymmetricGroup(4) and Dihedral(8) illustrate the nested series representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfUpperCentralSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfUpperCentralSeries(ordtbl) — class positions corresponding to the upper central series of the group of ordtbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: SymmetricGroup(4) -> [ [1] ], Dihedral(8) -> [ [1,3], [1,2,3,4,5] ].

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfSolvableRadical
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfSolvableRadical(ordtbl) — positions of classes forming the solvable radical of the group of ordtbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example ClassPositionsOfSolvableRadical(CharacterTable("2.A5")) -> [1,2].

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfSupersolvableResiduum
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfSupersolvableResiduum(ordtbl) — positions of classes corresponding to the supersolvable residuum of the group of ordtbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: SymmetricGroup(4) -> [1,3].

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfPCore
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfPCore(ordtbl, p) — positions of classes corresponding to the p-core (PCore) of the group of ordtbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example ClassPositionsOfPCore(CharacterTable("Symmetric",4),2) -> [1,3]; for p=3 -> [1].

rubrics_metrics.name: ClassPositionsOfNormalClosure
rubrics_metrics.description: ClassPositionsOfNormalClosure(ordtbl, classes) — sorted list of positions of all conjugacy classes of ordtbl that form the normal closure of the conjugacy classes at positions in classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example ClassPositionsOfNormalClosure(CharacterTable("Symmetric",4), [1,4]) -> [1,3,4].

rubrics_metrics.name: PrimeBlocks
rubrics_metrics.description: PrimeBlocks(ordtbl, p) / PrimeBlocksOp(ordtbl, p) / ComputedPrimeBlockss(tbl) — for ordinary character table ordtbl and prime p, PrimeBlocks returns a record with components block (assignment of irreducible characters to p-blocks), defect (defect of each block), height (height of each irreducible in its block), relevant (class positions needed to decide block membership), centralcharacter (central character values restricted to relevant positions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: two ordinary irreducible characters are in same p-block if images of their central characters are equal modulo any maximal ideal containing p; for |G|=p^a m, defect d of a block is exponent such that p^{a-d} is largest p-power dividing degrees of all characters in block; height of character χ is largest h with p^h dividing χ(1)/p^{a-d}. Default method stores computed values in ComputedPrimeBlockss and calls PrimeBlocksOp as needed. If InfoCharacterTable level ≥ 2, defects and heights are printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: SameBlock
rubrics_metrics.description: SameBlock(p, omega1, omega2, relevant) — returns true if central characters omega1 and omega2 (or their value lists) are equal modulo any maximal ideal in ring of algebraic integers containing ideal spanned by p, when restricted to positions in relevant; false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to decide block membership from central characters and the 'relevant' positions returned by PrimeBlocks. Example calls show SameBlock(2, omega[1], omega[2], pbl.relevant) -> true.

rubrics_metrics.name: BlocksInfo
rubrics_metrics.description: BlocksInfo(modtbl) — for a Brauer character table modtbl returns a list of records, one per block, with components defect, ordchars (positions of ordinary characters in block relative to Irr(OrdinaryCharacterTable(modtbl))), modchars (positions of Brauer characters in block relative to IBr(modtbl)), and optional components basicset, decmat (decomposition matrix), decinv, brauertree (if defect 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decomposition matrix stored when DecompositionMatrix is called; basicset is a maximally linearly independent restriction set. Example shows BlocksInfo(CharacterTable("L3(2)") mod 2) with two block records including basicset and decinv.

rubrics_metrics.name: DecompositionMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: DecompositionMatrix(modtbl[, blocknr]) — returns decomposition matrix of Brauer table modtbl (rows indexed by ordinary irreducibles of underlying ordinary table, columns by irreducible Brauer characters); with blocknr returns decomposition matrix for that block and stores it in BlocksInfo(modtbl)[blocknr].decmat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ordinary irreducible is in block i iff all characters before the first character of same block lie in i-1 different blocks. An irreducible Brauer character is in block i if it has nonzero scalar product with an ordinary irreducible in block i. DecompositionMatrix uses general Decomposition function. Examples illustrate full matrix and per-block matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeXStringDecompositionMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: LaTeXStringDecompositionMatrix(modtbl[, blocknr][, options]) — returns a string of LaTeX code to nicely print a decomposition matrix; options record may set phi, chi labels, collabels, rowlabels, nrows, ncols and can provide decmat directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults: phi='{\\tt Y}', chi='{\\tt X}', and default subscripts lists of positions. nrows/ncols cause chunking into arrays if present. If decmat bound in options it is used directly. Atlas-compatible labels constructed for Atlas tables via AtlasLabelsOfIrreducibles when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index (for two character tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Index(tbl, subtbl) — returns quotient of Size(tbl) / Size(subtbl). Containment of underlying groups is not checked, so distinction between Index and IndexNC is not made for character tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to compute index-like quotient between tables' Sizes; does not verify subgroup relation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsInternallyConsistent
rubrics_metrics.description: IsInternallyConsistent(tbl) — checks internal consistency of stored attribute values for ordinary and Brauer character tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ordinary tables checks consistency (if stored) among: Size, SizesCentralizers, SizesConjugacyClasses; SizesCentralizers and OrdersClassRepresentatives; ComputedPowerMaps and OrdersClassRepresentatives; SizesCentralizers and Irr (first orthogonality relation); Irr (first orthogonality). For Brauer tables checks: Size, SizesCentralizers, SizesConjugacyClasses; SizesCentralizers and OrdersClassRepresentatives; ComputedPowerMaps and OrdersClassRepresentatives; Irr closure under complex conjugation and Frobenius map. Returns true if no inconsistency, otherwise prints inconsistencies (if InfoWarning level ≥ 1) and returns false.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPSolvableCharacterTable
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPSolvableCharacterTable(tbl, p) / IsPSolubleCharacterTable(tbl, p) and related operations/attributes — corresponds to IsPSolvable for the group of tbl; p is prime or 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default method stores computed values in ComputedIsPSolvableCharacterTables at position p and calls IsPSolvableCharacterTableOp to compute unknown values. Used to determine p-solvability property from table data.
